clips.text: Perhaps the wind. Perhaps a ghost. I'd rather not know.
The detective found a clue under the carpet.
Welcome, new student. I am Eleanor, the archivist.
journey
Whoever did this knew exactly which book to take.
guard
Then the forest will stay silent. But I will remember you.
Whoever reads the book controls the archive.
The gates will open at midnight, when the bell rings twelve times.
brave
You said you hadn't seen anyone. Is that the whole truth?
trust
Then who rang the bell?
We found the key.
archive
You walk back with the amulet. The academy is safe, but tonight the forest is silent.

The footprints lead to the Archmage's Archives, where the academy keeps the books that must never be read aloud. One shelf is empty, and the dust around a clean, book-shaped gap has barely been disturbed.
All the windows are locked from inside, and the bell is far too heavy for the wind to move.
welcome
"Thank you, young one," says the spirit.
The council asks how the thief knew which book to take.
Only a brave student enters the tower at night.
moonlight
The ancient map shows a hidden door.
On the dusty stairs you find footprints. They are small, and they lead up — but none of them come down again.
rope
Our journey to the forgotten tower begins tonight.
I am old and very wise. I sleep in winter and wake up in spring. What am I?
The trees begin to sing. The forest thanks you, and the academy is safe.
The council takes the book back. Corwin is sent away from the academy, and the archives are sealed for another hundred years.
book
I am sorry. The academy needs it.
Had I known the tower was open, I would have sealed the archives myself.
cellar
Corwin returns the book and confesses. Eleanor forgives him, and the bell of the Tower of Echoes never rings again.
If the guard had stayed awake, the thief would not have entered.
The stairs are dark. The guard is nervous and keeps looking at the floor.
It is night. You open the big door of the Forgotten Academy. Inside, there are many old books.
"Who wrote the letter that sent you to the tower?" asks the spirit. "Show me."
…I fell asleep for an hour. When I woke up, the door had been opened.
I found it under the tower. Why is it yours?
whisper
There is a hidden room behind the bookshelf.
The guard insists that nobody went into the tower tonight.
seal
Find the rune stone with the letter R, then the glowing mushrooms next to it.
The raven is waiting at the old crossroads, near the broken bridge.
The violet ink leads to Eleanor's own apprentice, Corwin. He is waiting by the door with the book in his hands, shaking.
forest
Corwin confesses — and the night guard, who also told you the truth, stands beside him. Eleanor makes them both keepers of the tower, and at last the echoes fall silent.
The amulet glows in the dark. A narrow path leads into the Whispering Forest. The trees are tall and quiet.
Three weeks later, a bell rings at midnight in the Tower of Echoes — a tower that has been locked for a hundred years. Nobody in the academy has the key.
polite
The door opens only at midnight.
Students must be quiet in the library.
shadow
antique
mercy
library
The guard raised his lantern in the dark corridor.
Please read the first rule of the library.
footprints
hidden
I've been standing at this door since sunset, and I haven't seen anyone go in.
Stop, young one. That amulet belongs to the forest.
council
quiet
echo
I only wanted to understand the spell that had sealed the tower.
wise
Every evening the old librarian climbs the stairs and rings the bell.
Hello! Nice to meet you.
The next evening, Eleanor is not in the library. On her desk there is a letter with a wax seal.
confess
ancient
Go north and follow the sound of water.
When the bell rang, the guard ___.
You read the letter again. Under the seal, in very small letters: "Trust the owl, not the crown."
Eleanor told the council that she had never let a student into the archives.
Answer my riddle, and I will show you.
patient
lantern
clue
The spirit smiles: "You trusted the owl." Eleanor steps out from the trees. She was the forest's friend all along, and now you are her apprentice.
The spirit holds out its hand. "Eleanor hid the amulet to keep it safe. Give it back, and the forest will sing again."
Before my riddle, tell me: why did you come to the forest?
Then it was someone who knows these shelves as well as I do.
The seal shows an owl and a crescent moon.
The key is cold in your hand. The cellar is far below the tower, and the night is long.
The ancient walls whisper forgotten secrets.
Look for the room where the moon never shines.
The bell has not rung for a hundred years.
Then put the book back, and tell Eleanor the truth yourself.
